newsitem.title: UK: Australia 96 sugar output seen at 5.3 mt - millers.
newsitem.headline: Australia 96 sugar output seen at 5.3 mt - millers.

text.p: Australia should produce 5.30 million tonnes of sugar in the 1996 calendar year, up from 4.99 million a year previously, the general manager of the Australian Sugar Milling Council said on Wednesday.
Speaking at a two-day seminar hosted by the International Sugar Organization (ISO), John Desmarchelier said 1996 production of cane was forecast at 40.00 million tonnes after 37.37 million in 1995.

"With a relatively stable domestic consumption...the rise in production has been directed towards export markets," he said. "Over 85 percent of Australia's production is exported and, with expected growth in sugar production, this proportion is likely to increase to about 90 percent," Desmarchelier said.
He gave no details about when this rise might take place.
Australia was among the world's top four exporters of sugar along with Brazil, Thailand and the European Union.
According to ISO data, the bulk of its raws exports are directed towards Canada, China, Japan, Korea and Malaysia.

Desmarchelier said domestic consumption represented only about 15 percent of sugar output and reached 919,000 tonnes in 1995. But with a steady population growth, consumption had increased by 100,000 tonnes raw value over the last decade and reached approximately 50 kg per capita.
